item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I've just joined the site! My answer to the random question of the month is; my random thoughts seem to be SCP related lately, for example how you could use them, or sometimes how I could write a story about them.

I discovered SCP as my husband introduced me, I had seen a few videos mention it on YouTube but wasn't exactly sure what it was. After hearing him explain it I was instantly intrigued. I've been using the SCP reader app on my phone, I started from the beginning (SCP-001) and I'm currently on SCP-069. I have a lot to read but I'm loving it so much I don't care. I'm also a writer myself and I'd like to try my hand at writing my own SCP eventually. Which is why I chose this thread, I wasn't 100% sure which to post in. I also plan to vote on other SCP articles/tales etc. Some of my other hobbies include; video games, colouring, reading, and learning.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello my dudes :)

Very pleased to be a part of this wonderfully creative community. I have been a fan of the SCPverse for a number of years but only recently decided to join the site itself, as i've been having a hankering to write an entry of my own!

I cannae remember just how I stumbled upon the foundation, I imagine it was through some anomolous means ;)

I am from the UK and I wish to bring an anglo slant to my writing, as there's absolutely tons of folklore and legends over here to pull from (Black Beast of Dartmoor, Loch Ness Monster, Kentish Apeman). My favourite horror often has a comedic tinge which I believe can be very effective for heightening fear and dread (American Werewolf In London, for example).

As well as a love of old school horror movies and dark fantasy, I also love music, art and nature and spend a lot of my time drawing and writing music. I may start a series of SCP concept art at some point!

Thanks for accepting me into this community of utter weirdos, you're all fab 😁

Kind regards, The Albatross x

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
This is probably like the third re-introduction I've done in my entire stint here but, I figured I'd do another one because I'm becoming more active again, plus I finally got an account with my proper handle! (My old one was This Is War)

Howdy, I'm War, I've been a part of the community for some 4 1/2 years now with varying levels in activity (mostly on IRC as War_). I'm finally starting to get on the writing side of things and working towards my first mainsite piece, so let that be a testament to the fact you don't have to immediately jump into writing when you first join!

I used to do crit sweeps as a junior critter (once upon a time) and still will occasionally critique drafts or pitches, though I can't offer greenlights.

Anyways, figured I'd drop in and say hi, 'cause even though I've been here a while my presence on the wiki is far smaller compared to my activity on IRC.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Greetings reasercher murphy! Glad to have you aboard the site. As for the sandbox, here is not the correct place to post that. You should read this post Idea forum Guide to get an idea of how to go through the process of adding your ideas to the site. Best of luck
As for writing, just make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you! For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-4200its a safe SCP that reads not quite as safe as you'd think.

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerened, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

Best of luck!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello TahskaAjuha! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It seems you are quite interested in contributing to the site, aren't you? That's awesome! It also seems like you are quite fast with the process - it's really good to see that you didn't get confused on that - a lot of new people do, but it looks like you did very well. Ideally, to get some more info on the resources the site dedicated to helping writers, you'll want to click that collapsible down below.

Speaking of which, let's click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
I'm a 39 year old Community Minister with a philosophy degree and a heavy interest in table top roleplaying games.

A couple of years ago I was volunteering to run roleplaying games at a local high school, and in creating a game setting a couple of the kids mentioning drawing on the SCP setting for influence. When I asked what that was they described it as a collaborative writing project, which I assumed was something they were working on for class. I didn't ask any follow up questions. Six months later I stumbled upon some SCP youtube videos (with some not-really SCP videos, like Sirenhead and creepypastas) and ended up watching quite a few of them, mostly The Volgun and Eastside Show. That's become part of my routine now, when folding laundry or on the treadmill.

I mentioned rpgs as a hobby, but they're also a significant part of my work. I use them extensively in my ministry, as a community building tool and as an educational tool. It was probably inevitable then that I'd end up running a game set in the (well 'an') SCP Universe, and started doing so last Monday. I'm in the process of creating a website for our 'SCP: Outpost 108' campaign. I have a question along those lines; I want to put up some useful intro links, and I was wondering what other people thought should go on that list of links. So far I have a link to each of the following: The SCP Wiki, The SCP Wikipedia page, the wiki glossary page, the wiki security levels page, and the wiki MTF page.

We're not using any of the specific established canons, so this is 'mainline' SCP stuff.
